idiom_name: application package exposing a Service struct with coarse methods; fine-grained collaborators as small consumer-declared interfaces
implementation_notes: Go replaces the class + declared interface + factory triad with a plain struct in a use-case package whose coarse methods orchestrate injected collaborators, and with interfaces declared by the consumer ('accept interfaces, return structs'): the facade's constructor takes small interfaces (type Quoter interface { Quote(ctx context.Context, sku string, qty int) (Quote, error) }) that the concrete repositories satisfy implicitly, so no implementer ever names the facade's contract. What is NOT replaced is the structure itself - a struct with methods over injected collaborators is the classic facade - which is why the notes here are about wiring rather than about a substitute idiom; there is no container, so the graph is assembled in main and context.Context carries the deadline and cancellation of the whole conversation. Keep the facade stateless and pass one context per operation; a struct field holding mutable request state would be shared across goroutines.
pitfalls: Interface satisfaction is implicit, so a collaborator of the wrong shape fails only where it is passed; keep constructors taking the interface (not the concrete type) so the compiler checks the wiring at the call site.
Swallowing errors (ignoring the returned error, or logging and continuing) breaks the workflow contract other Go code relies on; wrap with %w so callers can still inspect the cause.
A Service struct with mutable fields shared across goroutines races; keep request state in local variables and pass it through the call.
